21. EPILEPSY
•Maternal mortality10 Fold in WWE.

WWE: women with epilepsy.

•Incidence 0.5 – 1%

Types:

1.Tonic Clonic:
⇨Highest risk of SUDEP.
⇨Sudden loss of conscious and fell without warning symptoms.
2.Absence seizure.
⇨Worsening absence => risk of tonic – colonic.
3.Juvenile:
⇨Sudden Jerks -> falling of baby.
4.Focal seizure:
⇨Complex partial – with loss of consciousness.
⇨Simple partial – without unconsciousness.
•Involve Neurologist -> if diagnostic uncertainty.

No longer have Epilepsy:

1.Seizure free > 10 years.
2.Last 5 years without treatment.
3.Childhood epilepsy syndrome.

Pre – pregnancy counselling:

•Folic acid 5mg 3m0 before – continue throughout pregnancy.
•Monotherapy or less teratogenic drugs.
•Avoid sodium valproate -> change to safe drug
•Multi drug change to Monotherapy
•Lamotrigine, carbamazepine – No effect on Neurodevelopment.
⇨Lowest effective dose of most appropriate AED 2/3rd = No fit in pregnancy.

< 1 year of last fit => close monitoring.

Safe => lamotrigine, carbamazepine, levetiracetam.

Anomalies:

•1 drug = 6 – 7%.
•2 drugs = 15%.
•3 drugs = 50%.

Anomalies Risk:

1.WWE = 28%.
2.Sodium valproate = 10.7%.
3.Poly therapy = 16.8%.
4.WWE with previous affected child = 16.8%.
⇨Na – valproate = NTD, facial cleft, hypospadias.
⇨Phenobarbital + phenytoin cardiac defects.
⇨Phenytoin + carbamazepine = cleft palate, cleft lip

Effect of Epilepsy on Pregnancy:

•Seizure free – 67%
•ed frequency – 17%.
•Frequency – 16%.
•Intrapartum seizure – 3.5%.
•Status Epilepticus – 2%.

ANC:

•Anomaly Scan 18 – 21 weeks.

Drugs Monitoring:

•In special circumstances not routinely lamotrigine level up to 70% => risk of seizures.

Current practice: to adjust the dose is

•Either monitor regularly
•Or adjust according to clinical features

 

Maternal Monitoring:

•Sleep.
•Dehydration.
•AED adherence.
•Seizure type and frequency.

No role of antenatal vitamin K to mother, given only to high risk of Haemorrhagic disease of new born.

Delivery according to obstetric indications.

Regular dose steroids (in enzyme inducers double dose).

Fetal:

•Serial growth scan from 28 weeks.

IPC:

•1 – 2% risk of fits during labour
•Avoid precipitating factors – continue AED.
⇨Clobazam – long-acting benzodiazepine

 

 

If risk of fits is highest.

⇨Prophylactic clobazam during Labor:
1.Fits in previous labor.
2.History of fit with stress.
3.History of recurrent fits
⇨Benzodiazepine – drug of choice during labor.
⇨CEFM – high risk of fits or after fits.
⇨Intermittent – low risk pts (10year fit free or 5 years without mediation).

Seizures:

•> 5 min => high risk for progression to status.
•1% individuals with epilepsy present with status.
•Medical emergency

 

•Left lateral.
•Lorazepam/ Diazepam/ Midazolam

Not controlled

•Phenytoin.

Uncontrolled seizures lead to

hypertonus uterus:

- Tocolytics

-CEFM

Abnormal CTG not recovering to normal after 5 min or recurrent fits are indications of Emergency c/s

Anaesthesia/ Analgesia

Avoid:

-Pethidine.
-Ketamine.
-Sevoflurane.

Use:

-No, TENS,

Regional anaesthesia, diamorphine.

PNC:

•Vitamin K injection to Neonates.
•Continue AED
-Sodium Valproate, Carbamazepine, phenytoin => minimum transfer in milk.
-Lamotrigine, Levetiracetam, topiramate => transfer in milk.
•If AED ed during pregnancy => reviewed within 10 days of delivery to avoid toxicity.

 

⇨Highest risk of fits => postpartum.

1 – 2% postpartum

3.5% (according to TOG article).

B.F:

-Lamotrigine 50% excretion in milk – so breast feeding before taking dose.
-Other drugs 3 – 5% excretion.

Contraception:

•IUD, Mirena, DMPA – not affected by Enzyme inducers, carbamazepine, topiramate, phenytoin, phenobarbital
•COC, POP, implants, Patch, ring – affected by enzyme inducers.

Dose of Estradiol to 70mcg and reduce pill free interval from 7 – 4 days.

Offer all Methods to Women taken:

⇨Sodium Valproate, levetiracetam, gabapentin, vigabatrin, pregabalin.
•Emergency Contraception=> IUD or 3mg LNG.

Don’t offer UPA.

•COC lamotrigine level 25 – 70% => fits.

Enzyme inducers: CP3T

•Carbamazepine, phenytoin.
•Primidone phenobarbital.
•Topiramate.

Non-Inducers: SL2

•Sodium Valproate, levetiracetam, lamotrigine.

Non – epileptic Seizure disorders:

•Psychogenic most common
•Associated with
1.Prolonged repeated seizures without cyanosis
2.Resistance to eye opening
3.Down going planters
4.Persistence of +ve conjunctival reflex
